## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The cow and the dead person  (`#the-cow-and-the-dead`)

Cited ayat: 2:67-73

> **2:67** وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا۟ بَقَرَةً قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
>
> **2:68** قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِىَ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌۢ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ فَٱفْعَلُوا۟ مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ

>
> **2:73** فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:67): Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow; they asked whether he was making a mockery of them, and he said he sought refuge in God from being among the ignorant.

**c2** (2:68): They asked him to call on his Lord to make clear what kind of cow it was; he replied that his Lord says it is a cow neither old nor young but in between, and told them to do as they were commanded.

**c3** (2:69): They asked about its colour; he replied that his Lord says it is a yellow cow, bright in colour, pleasing to those who look.

**c4** (2:70): They asked once more, saying that cows looked alike to them and that, God willing, they would be guided.

**c5** (2:71): He replied that his Lord says it is a cow not broken in to turn the earth or water the field, sound, with no mark in it; they said he had now brought the truth, and they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it.

**c6** (2:72): God reminds them that they killed a person and fell into dispute about it, and that God was bringing out what they were hiding.

**c7** (2:73): God told them to strike him with a part of it, and said that in this way God gives life to the dead and shows them His signs, so that they might understand.

### One-minute summary

Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow, and they asked more and more about it before they did it [c1][c2][c5]. The ayat then recall a person they had killed and disputed about, and God told them to strike him with a part of it [c6][c7].

### Complete story

Musa told his people that God commands them to slaughter a cow [c1]. They asked whether he was making a mockery of them, and he said he sought refuge in God from being among the ignorant [c1].

They asked him to call on his Lord to make clear what kind of cow it was [c2]. He replied that it was neither old nor young but in between, and told them to do as they were commanded [c2]. They asked about its colour, and he replied that it was a yellow cow, bright in colour, pleasing to those who look [c3].

They asked once more, saying that cows looked alike to them and that, God willing, they would be guided [c4]. He replied that it was a cow not broken in to turn the earth or water the field, sound, with no mark in it [c5]. They said he had now brought the truth, and they slaughtered it, though they almost did not do it [c5].

God reminds them that they killed a person and fell into dispute about it, and that God was bringing out what they were hiding [c6]. God told them to strike him with a part of it, and said that in this way God gives life to the dead and shows them His signs, so that they might understand [c7].

### Deep study

Each answer from Musa begins by saying that his Lord says it, so the descriptions are given as coming from God and not from Musa [c2][c3][c5]. Their questions come one after another, and the last description is the narrowest [c2][c3][c5]. The ayat end the account by stating what the event shows: God gives life to the dead and shows His signs so that people might understand [c7].

### Kids mode

Musa told his people that God told them to slaughter a cow [c1]. They kept asking what kind of cow it should be, and in the end they slaughtered it, though they almost did not [c2][c5]. God said that this showed how He gives life to the dead [c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the people asked again and again before doing what they were told, and that the account sets this beside the plain instruction to do as they were commanded [c2][c5]. Another is that the ayat close on understanding, not on the cow itself [c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the person was, who killed him, where or when, and why the people disputed about it.
- Not established: which part of the cow was used, what happened when the person was struck, or what the dead person said or did; the ayah says only that God gives life to the dead in this way.
- Not established: how the order of the ayat relates to the order of events; the killing and the dispute are recalled after the cow is slaughtered.
- The verses call them his people and do not name them.
